title: Explorer parameters on large instances, long runs (round 1)
question: Which explorer settings (count, rate, heuristic exponent, deposit) give the lowest cost on the large Table I instances when runs are long (1,500 iterations)?
hypothesis: The defaults found at 600 iterations (2 explorers, rate 0.05, beta 0.5, deposit 0.05) stay good in long runs; a smaller deposit (0.02) may be better, since larger deposits helped less at 600 iterations.
analysisPlan: Final best cost as the paired gap to the plain colony n0 on the same seeds (same instance and repeat): mean, 95% interval, exact Wilcoxon, Holm over the 10 explorer settings. Secondary: anytime gap curves (trace.jsonl, every 50 iterations) and solution diversity (metric 'diversity': mean share of patients whose predecessor or hospital differs between two ants), used as tie-breakers and as a check that a gain comes with kept diversity. This is round 1 of a two-round race: seeds 0-4, 15 paired runs per setting. Runs 1-31 of this experiment were made by the study script (sens/Tune.java, same code and seeds) and imported; the catalog path was checked to reproduce that script's runs exactly.
decisionRule: Round 2 (seeds 5-9) gets every setting not clearly beaten: drop a setting if it is worse than the best round-1 setting with a paired Wilcoxon p < 0.05 on the 15 paired runs; always keep the default (n2_r0.05_b0.5_d0.05). After round 2, choose the setting with the lowest mean gap over 30 runs; if it is not significantly better than the default (paired p < 0.05), keep the default. Among statistically equal settings prefer the one with higher final diversity.
